about: The priest joins his hands and prays for a while for the living whom he intends to remember. The prayer then embraces all who are present and names its intentions: the redemption of their souls, the hope of salvation, and their well-being.

s01.translation: Remember, Lord, Your servants and handmaids

s02.narrative: The priest joins his hands and prays a while in silence for those he means to remember, then spreads his hands and goes on.

s03.translation: and all gathered here, whose faith and devotion are known to You. For them we offer to You:

s04.translation: or they themselves offer You this sacrifice of praise, for themselves and all who are dear to them: for the redemption of their souls, in hope of salvation and well-being,

s05.translation: and paying their vows to You, the eternal God, living and true.

w004.function: Genitive plural with the conjunction “-que” attached.

w008.function: A participle used as a noun in the genitive plural.

w013.function: The shared verb of “fides cognita” and “nota devótio”.

w027.function: The phrase “sacrifícium laudis” occurs in Ps 49:14 and 106:22.

w029.function: “pro” (w028) requires the ablative. The form “se” itself marks neither number nor gender.

w030.function: Ablative plural after “pro” (w028), with the conjunction “-que” attached.

w033.function: Ablative after “pro” (w032): “for the redemption of their souls”.

w038.function: A genitive dependent on “spe” (w037), coordinated with “incolumitátis” (w040).

w043.function: The phrase “vota réddere” occurs in Ps 115:14 and 18.

w047.function: Dative marking the recipient of the vows. The phrase “Deo vivo et vero” occurs in 1 Thess 1:9.
